# Widget Types

`type` in `widgets.json` selects the renderer. Pick the type that matches the **shape of the data and the user task**, not the type that's easiest to implement.

## Catalog

The types FINOS Workspace renders itself:

<!-- generated:types -->
| Type | Use case | Endpoint returns | Method | Params go in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `markdown` | Prose, generated commentary, formatted text | A markdown string, as text or as JSON with the string at `data.dataKey` | GET or POST | query, header, body, or the path |
| `html` | A report, page or visualization the backend renders itself | An HTML document as text | GET or POST | query, header, body, or the path |
| `newsfeed` | Articles and updates, each with a title, an excerpt and a full text | A JSON array of articles, or JSON with the array at `data.dataKey` | GET or POST | query, header, body, or the path |
| `pdf` | A document the user reads page by page | The PDF (`application/pdf`), or JSON with its `data_format` and a base64 `content` or a `url` | GET or POST | query, header, body, or the path |
| `iframe` | An existing web page | Nothing: the endpoint is the page's URL, which the browser opens | GET | query, or the path |
<!-- /generated:types -->

A widget plugin can add types. A plugin is installed for the deployment and enabled per organization by its administrators, so the types a user can use depend on their organization: `workspace://specs/widgets-json-schema` is the schema in force for the signed-in user, with those types. A widget of a type nothing renders for the user is left out of their catalog, and FINOS Workspace names it in a warning when the backend is connected.

> Use the exact type string. Don't invent aliases.

## Use-case → type quick selector

| Data shape | Type |
|------------|------|
| Long-form prose, generated commentary, a list of findings | `markdown` |
| A report with its own layout, styling, tables or graphics that the backend renders | `html` |
| Articles, announcements or updates with a title and a body | `newsfeed` |
| A document, filing or report that exists as a PDF | `pdf` |
| An application or page that already has a URL | `iframe` |

## Choose this, not that

- **Prose goes to `markdown`, not `html`.** Markdown picks up the FINOS Workspace's theme and typography; use `html` only when you need layout or graphics markdown cannot express.
- **Articles go to `newsfeed`, not `markdown`.** `newsfeed` shows the list with title, date and author, a search box and each article's full text on demand; a `markdown` widget would be one long page.
- **A document that exists as a file goes to `pdf`, not a link inside `markdown`.**
- **A page you do not control goes to `iframe`, not a copy of its HTML.** Some sites refuse to be embedded; if the page stays blank, serve it from your own backend as `html` instead.
- **Dates, numbers and flags are params, not text.** Pick the right param `type` (`workspace://specs/widget-parameters`) so the user gets a date picker or a toggle instead of a text box.

## `html` widgets

The endpoint's response is shown in a sandboxed frame. Scripts run only when the deployment enables HTML script execution, so a report should read correctly without them. The widget follows the FINOS Workspace theme only if the endpoint honors a `theme` query parameter (`dark` or `light`), which FINOS Workspace sends.

If the HTML is generated from data rows, set `"raw": true` on the widget and have the endpoint return those rows as JSON when it is called with `raw=true`. FINOS Workspace then shows a toggle between the report and its data, and the AI Agent reads the rows instead of parsing the HTML (see `workspace://overview/ai-agent-contract`).

## `newsfeed` widgets

The endpoint returns a JSON array. If the array sits inside an object, set `"data": { "dataKey": "path.to.articles" }` on the widget.

```json
[
  {
    "title": "Rates held steady",
    "date": "2026-03-04T09:30:00Z",
    "author": "A. Writer",
    "excerpt": "The committee left rates unchanged on Wednesday.",
    "body": "# Rates held steady\n\nThe committee left rates unchanged..."
  }
]
```

`title` and `body` are required for a useful article; `date` is an ISO 8601 string. `body` is markdown, shown in a dialog when the user opens the article, where they can also add it to the dashboard as a `markdown` widget. The user's search box filters by `title` and `excerpt`, so write an `excerpt` that says what the article covers.

## `pdf` widgets

The endpoint answers in one of three ways:

- `Content-Type: application/pdf` and the file as the body.
- `Content-Type: application/json` and `{ "data_format": { "data_type": "pdf", "filename": "report.pdf" }, "content": "<base64 of the file>" }`.
- `Content-Type: application/json` and `{ "data_format": { "data_type": "pdf", "filename": "report.pdf" }, "url": "<where the file can be fetched>" }`.

## What this spec does not cover

- Widget-level metadata fields — see `workspace://specs/widgets-json`.
- Param types and option sources — see `workspace://specs/widget-parameters`.
- Layout coordinates — see `workspace://specs/apps-json` and `workspace://specs/layout-grid`.

# `widgets.json` Spec

`widgets.json` is the metadata contract that tells FINOS Workspace which widgets your backend offers, what type each one is, and which endpoint serves its data.

## Top-level shape

`widgets.json` is a JSON **object**. Keys are widget ids, values are widget definitions:

```json
{
  "weekly_summary": { "...widget definition..." },
  "audit_report":   { "...widget definition..." }
}
```

Returning a JSON array is the most common mistake here — FINOS Workspace will reject it. Widget ids are referenced by app layouts (the `i` field in `apps.json` layout items), so they must be stable.

## Widget definition fields

Each value is an object with these keys and no others:

<!-- generated:widget-fields -->
| Field | Required | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | Yes | `markdown`, `html`, `newsfeed`, `pdf`, `iframe`, or a plugin type enabled for the organization | What renders the widget |
| `name` | Yes | text, at most 200 characters | The title the widget shows |
| `description` | Yes | text, at most 4,000 characters | What the widget shows; the catalog shows it, and the AI Agent finds widgets by it |
| `endpoint` | Yes | text, at most 2,048 characters | A path or an absolute URL with no `?` and no `#` (a static query value is a param with show: false) |
| `method` | No | `GET`, `POST` | How FINOS Workspace calls the endpoint: GET (the default) or POST, which a param `in: body` needs |
| `category` | No | text, at most 100 characters | The group the catalog lists the widget under |
| `subCategory` | No | text, at most 100 characters | The subgroup within the category |
| `source` | No | text, at most 100 characters or list of text, at most 16 | Where the data comes from: a label, or a list of labels |
| `showTitle` | No | `true` or `false` | False leaves the title off the widget |
| `params` | No | list of params | The widget's parameters; an item that is a list of params is one row of the parameter bar |
| `gridData` | No | object | The default size on a dashboard, in grid units: `w` of 40 columns, and `h` rows |
| `staleTime` | No | number, 1,000 to 10,000,000,000 or `false` | Milliseconds a response is reused before it is fetched again; false fetches every time |
| `refetchInterval` | No | number, 1,000 to 10,000,000,000 or `false` or text, at most 100 characters or `null` | Fetch again every so many milliseconds, or on a 5-field cron schedule; false never |
| `dataUpdateDisplay` | No | text, at most 100 characters | When the data changes, as a 5-field cron expression shown to the user |
| `runButton` | No | `true` or `false` | The widget fetches only when the user clicks Run |
| `disableRetrievalForCopilot` | No | `true` or `false` | Keeps the widget's data from the AI Agent; such a widget has no `mcp_tool` |
| `exportable` | No | `true` or `false` | False removes Export from the widget's menu |
| `mcp_tool` | No | object | The MCP tool of this backend the AI Agent uses to query what the widget shows: a server named in this backend's apps.json mcpServers, and the tool |
| `data` | No | object | `dataKey`, `rawDataKey` and `rawType` where the type has `raw`, and for a plugin's type the configuration its plugin defines |
| `raw` | No | `true` or `false` | Only for `html` and plugin types. The endpoint also answers `raw=true` with the rows the widget shows, as JSON: the AI Agent and MCP get those rows, and the widget's rows button shows them |
| `requires_auth` | No | `true` or `false` | Only for `iframe`. The page needs the backend connection's credentials. The browser then opens it through the FINOS Workspace API, which adds them, in a sandbox without storage. For trusted pages only: the API checks this declaration itself |
| `storage` | No | object | Only for `iframe`. `mcpUrl`: an MCP server of the page's own, connected for the widget without the backend's credentials |
<!-- /generated:widget-fields -->

The contract defines every key and bounds every value. A key it does not define is ignored: the widget loads without it, and FINOS Workspace names the key under the backend's unrecognized fields. A value outside its bounds leaves the widget out, and FINOS Workspace names the widget and the path of each problem when the backend is connected; the other widgets load. `workspace://specs/widgets-json-schema` is the JSON Schema in force for the signed-in user, for an editor or a test. Set `runButton` only for heavy work (more than 5 seconds).

## `gridData` is a hint, not the layout

`gridData` is the default placement when a widget is dragged onto a dashboard from the catalog. It is *not* the layout used by an app template — that lives in `apps.json` under `tabs[].layout[]`. Don't try to express tabs or coordinates inside `widgets.json`.

Common mistakes:

- Returning an array instead of an object.
- A `type` nothing renders for the user: the widget is left out of their catalog.
- A key the table does not list, such as `defaultViz`, `widgetId` or `widgetType`: the widget is refused.
- A `?` or `#` in `endpoint`: a static query value is a param with a default value and `"show": false`.

## The request

`endpoint` is a path on the backend, or an absolute URL, with no `?` and no `#`; it does not have to match the widget id. For the current param values FINOS Workspace builds one request:

1. **URL.** A `{name}` placeholder in `endpoint` takes the value of the param `name`, encoded as one path segment; the request is not sent while it has no value. Each param with `in: "query"`, or no `in`, is appended to the query.
2. **Headers.** Each param with `in: "header"`, named by its `paramName`. The API adds the backend connection's credentials, `X-Workspace-User`, `X-Workspace-Identity` and, when the deployment turns it on, the identity provider's ID token.
3. **Body.** With `"method": "POST"`, the params with `in: "body"` as one JSON object, `{ "<paramName>": <value> }`, sent as `Content-Type: application/json`.
4. **FINOS Workspace's own query values.** `theme` (`dark` or `light`) for `markdown`, `html`, `iframe` and plugin types, and `raw=true` for the raw view of an `html` widget. They are reserved names for those types.

An empty value is not sent, in any place; `0` and `false` are. How each kind of value is written is in `workspace://specs/widget-parameters`.

The FINOS Workspace API sends the request, whatever the method and the params are, so the backend needs no CORS settings. See `workspace://contract/backend`.

## The MCP tool link

A widget can name the MCP tool of its own backend that the AI Agent uses to query what the widget shows:

```json
"mcp_tool": {
  "mcp_server": "Team data",
  "tool_id": "get_team_report",
  "args": { "team_id": "$team", "period": "$period" }
}
```

- `mcp_server` is the `name` of a server in the `mcpServers` of this backend's `apps.json` (`workspace://specs/apps-json`), compared exactly; never a URL. A widget whose `mcp_server` names no declared server is refused, so a backend with no `apps.json` cannot use the key.
- `tool_id` is the tool's name on that server, compared exactly.
- `args` maps the tool's arguments to the widget's params: `"$<paramName>"` is the param's current value, which must be declared, and anything else is a literal. Without `args`, an argument named like a param takes its value.
- The link enables nothing: the agent is told of it only while the tool is in its tool list (the server connected and enabled, the tool switched on, granted to the user, and MCP tools on for the agent).
- When the agent calls the tool, the result is cited as this widget, with the call's arguments turned back into its params through `args`. Several widgets may name one tool: the one whose literal `args` all equal the call's, with the most literals, is cited.
- A widget with `disableRetrievalForCopilot: true` cannot have `mcp_tool`.
- The server decides what a call may do; make the tool a read-only query.

## Example shape

```json
{
  "weekly_summary": {
    "name": "Weekly Summary",
    "description": "The week's activity for one team, as written commentary",
    "type": "markdown",
    "endpoint": "/summary",
    "gridData": { "w": 20, "h": 12 },
    "params": [
      { "paramName": "team", "type": "endpoint", "label": "Team", "description": "Team to summarize",
        "optionsEndpoint": "/teams" }
    ]
  },
  "team_report": {
    "name": "Team report",
    "description": "Report for one team and period",
    "type": "markdown",
    "method": "POST",
    "endpoint": "/teams/{team}/report",
    "params": [
      { "paramName": "team", "type": "endpoint", "label": "Team", "value": "platform",
        "optionsEndpoint": "/teams/search", "optionsMethod": "POST", "optionsParams": { "active": true } },
      { "paramName": "period", "type": "text", "label": "Period", "value": "month" },
      { "paramName": "X-Region", "type": "text", "label": "Region", "value": "eu", "in": "header" },
      { "paramName": "filters", "type": "text", "label": "Filters", "value": "active", "in": "body" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`team_report` is sent as `POST <backend>/teams/platform/report?period=month&theme=dark`, with the header `X-Region: eu` and the body `{"filters":"active"}`. Its `team` choices come from `POST <backend>/teams/search` with the body `{"active":true}`.

## What this spec does not cover

- Choosing a widget type — see `workspace://specs/widget-types`.
- Authoring params — see `workspace://specs/widget-parameters`.
- Wiring layouts and parameter sync — see `workspace://specs/apps-json` and `workspace://specs/layout-grid`.
- Common validation errors — see `workspace://validation/common-errors`.

# Common Errors

The mistakes that catch real apps. When validation fails, walk this list before exploring.

## `widgets.json` shape

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `[widgets.json]: Invalid format`, with an `Expected` and a `Received` line | Top-level is `[ ... ]`, or a single widget instead of an object of widgets | Change to `{ "widget_id": { ... } }` |
| `missing \`name\`` (or `description`, `endpoint`) | A required key is absent | Add it |
| A widget's key listed under unrecognized fields | A key the contract does not define, such as `defaultViz`, `widgetId` or `widgetType`; the widget loads without it | Remove it; the keys are in `workspace://specs/widgets-json` |
| Widget missing from the catalog, with a warning that nothing renders its type | A typo, a type that nothing renders (such as `table`, `chart` or `metric`), or a plugin type not enabled for the organization | Use a built-in type, or ask an administrator to enable the plugin |
| `endpoint` must be a path or an absolute URL with no `?` and no `#` | A static query value in the endpoint | Make it a param with a default `value` and `"show": false` |
| `` `{xxx}` names no param of this widget `` | A placeholder in `endpoint` with no param of that name | Declare the param, or fix the placeholder |
| `` `xxx` fills a path placeholder, so it is sent nowhere else and declares no `in` `` | A path param with `in` | Remove its `in` |
| `Body params are sent only with "method": "POST"` | A param `in: body` on a `GET` widget | Set `"method": "POST"` |
| A header param refused | Its name is one a browser forbids or FINOS Workspace sets, or one the backend connection's credentials use | Rename it; the rules are in `workspace://specs/widget-parameters` |
| `` `xxx` is declared twice `` | Two params with one `paramName` | Rename one |
| Widget far too wide or too narrow on the dashboard | `gridData.w` does not fit the 40-column grid | Use `w` between 1 and 40 |
| Widget endpoint 404 | Path mismatch | Confirm `endpoint` matches a real route |

## `apps.json` shape

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `[tabs]: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined` | Missing or wrong tab structure | Each tab needs `id`, `name`, `layout` |
| App has no thumbnail | `img`, `img_dark`, and `img_light` are empty | Prefer a stable hosted image URL or serve a small SVG/PNG from `/thumbnails/{name}` |
| Creating a dashboard from the app fails with `Unable to create app because these widgets are unavailable: xxx` | Layout `i` doesn't match any widget id | Fix typo or align with `widgets.json` keys |
| `id` rejected | Top-level `id` doesn't match `^custom-.+` | Use `custom-<slug>` or omit `id` |

## Layout fields

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Widget never appears | Layout used `id` instead of `i` | Rename the key to `i` |
| Coordinates ignored | Layout used `gridData: {x,y,w,h}` | Use `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` directly on the layout item |

## Parameter groups

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Group exists, no widget joins | A layout item's `groups` does not contain the group's exact `name` | Make the `name` in `groups` and in each layout item the same text |
| Group exists but sync silently disabled | Group `type` doesn't match the underlying param shape | `param` for static `text+options`, `endpointParam` for `endpoint+optionsEndpoint` |
| Sync works for some widgets, not others | A widget is missing from the group's `widgetIds`, or its layout entry is missing `"groups": [...]`, or its widget config uses a different `paramName`/`optionsEndpoint` | Make all three places agree |

## Endpoint and route check

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Validate Widgets fails a route | The route answers `404` to the plain `OPTIONS` request that the API sends | Answer `OPTIONS` with `204` on every route in `widgets.json` (`workspace://contract/backend`) |
| Validate Widgets lists routes as not checked | The backend answers every `OPTIONS` request, whatever the path, so the check cannot tell a route from a path that does not exist | Answer `OPTIONS` with `404` on a path that does not exist (`workspace://contract/backend`) |
| A widget fails with the header `X-Workspace-Proxy-Error` | The API refused or could not make the request: `403` for a connection that is not a superuser's and is not a public `https` address, `502` when nothing answered | Use a public `https` address, or have a superuser add the connection |
| A widget shows "`xxx` needs a value" instead of its data | A path param, or a placeholder of `optionsEndpoint`, has no value | Give the param a default `value`, or choose one |
| The API cannot reach the backend | A connection that is not a superuser's must be a public `https` address, unless the stack runs with `MODE=local` | Serve the backend over public HTTPS, or develop on a local stack |
| 404 on widget endpoint | Path typo or missing route | Confirm the route is registered; match `endpoint` exactly |
| Wrong response shape | Endpoint returns the wrong kind of response for the widget type | `markdown` → string; `html` → HTML document; `newsfeed` → array of articles; `pdf` → file or base64 JSON |
| Garbled non-ASCII | JSON file read with OS locale (cp1252 on Windows) | Open files with `encoding="utf-8"` (Python) or your language's UTF-8 equivalent |

## When the doc and the validator disagree

Trust the running validator. FINOS Workspace's actual validator is the source of truth — adjust the files to match what it accepts, then update docs.

- **Preferred check** — `workspace_mcp`: `manage_backends(operation="add", url=...)` returns schema errors directly.
- **Browser check**: open Connections in the sidebar and choose Connect Backend. FINOS Workspace validates the backend and lists the invalid items.

See `workspace://guides/debug-app` for the full diagnostic order.

tools.description: Fetch the exact schema for one available widget. data_args_schema and ui_args_schema are closed JSON Schemas for the data_args and ui_args of create_widget and update_widget: a ui_args key or value they do not accept refuses the call, and a data_args value they do not accept is ignored with a warning. method is the widget's HTTP method, and each param's in says where its value goes in the widget's request: path, query, header or body. mcp_tool, when present, names the MCP tool of the widget's own backend that queries what the widget shows, and how its params fill the tool's arguments. The response includes grid_data when layout defaults or min/max constraints are defined for that widget. If a param returns requires_options_lookup=true, call get_params_options before using that param in create_widget or update_widget.
tools.name: get_widget_schema

origin.description: Widget origin. Pass origin exactly as returned by list_available_widgets.

tools.description: Request a fresh FINOS Workspace snapshot from the connected browser. Call this first when you need current dashboard state, dashboard identifiers across the workspace, or skill identifiers. The snapshot is intentionally compact: use list_available_widgets, get_widget_schema, and manage_dashboard for deeper follow-up inspection. dashboard_composition exposes deterministic tabs, layout coordinates, and groups for the current dashboard. If snapshot.skills lists a skill relevant to the request, call get_skill_content with its slug before composing.
tools.name: get_workspace_snapshot

tools.description: List widgets available to the current FINOS Workspace session. Returns deterministic widget identities for later get_widget_schema and create_widget calls. Each returned widget includes origin; pass origin to other widget tools exactly as returned by list_available_widgets. A blank origin means the catalog is invalid. Only the deterministic plain-create subset is returned: widgets that still require runtime-only bootstrap are intentionally excluded; use add_generative_widget for notes. Without filters the entire catalog is returned, which can be hundreds of widgets — prefer a filter when you know the source. Large unfiltered results return a compact index plus a result_ref resource with the full catalog.
tools.name: list_available_widgets

backend_id.description: Filter: backend UUID returned by manage_backends. Use backend_id when you have a UUID from manage_backends. Both filters can be passed together for a stricter match.

origin.description: Filter: friendly catalog label matched exactly (e.g. 'Options Activity Monitor'). Use origin when working from a snapshot.

tools.description: List, read, or instantiate FINOS Workspace apps (dashboard templates). There is no app update or delete through this MCP surface. Apps bundle tabs, widget layouts, parameter groups, and suggested prompts. Instantiating one is the programmatic equivalent of clicking an app in the gallery. For list, apps come from the user's own backends (type='backend'), apps shared through their organization (type='shared'), and saved apps they created or that were shared with them (type='saved'). Each app includes name, template_id, description, type, backend_id, backend_name, is_shared, and created_by. For read, requires app_name (or template_id); resolves across all app sources and returns the full app definition including tabs with layouts (or widgets for saved apps), parameter groups, and suggested prompts. For instantiate, requires app_name (or template_id); creates a fresh dashboard from the app template and returns its dashboard_id. Pass that dashboard_id to subsequent dashboard-targeting tools. Apps are defined by the apps.json a backend serves; to author one, read the workspace://app-builder/index resource.
tools.name: manage_apps

activate.description: For instantiate: defaults to true and routes the browser to the new dashboard.

app_name.description: App name for read and instantiate; either app_name or template_id is required.

backend_id.description: For list: omit to return every app the user can see; pass backend_id only to filter to one backend (own or shared). Use manage_backends operation='list' to discover backend_id values.

dashboard_name.description: For instantiate: optional name for the created dashboard.

operation.description: What to do with the apps.

template_id.description: App template id; alternative to app_name.

tools.description: Manage FINOS Workspace data backends (the connections that power widgets). For list, returns each backend with id, name, url, status, and widget/app/agent counts. For add, requires name and url. For update, requires backend_id and at least one of name, url, endpoint_headers. For refresh, requires backend_id; re-fetches widgets and templates from the backend URL. For remove, requires backend_id. To author or debug a custom backend's widgets.json or apps.json, read the workspace://app-builder/index resource; it links the specs, minimal working examples, and validation/common-errors.
tools.name: manage_backends

backend_id.description: Backend UUID from manage_backends operation='list'. Required for update, refresh, and remove.

key.description: The name of the header or of the query parameter.

location.description: Whether it goes in the headers or in the query.

value.description: The value that the backend's endpoints receive.

endpoint_headers.description: Array of {"key", "value", "location"} objects where location is "headers" (default) or "query".

operation.description: What to do with the backends.

validate_widgets.description: For add: defaults to true and surfaces a warning if widgets fail to load.

tools.description: Create, read, or update one FINOS Workspace dashboard. Dashboard deletion is not available through this MCP surface. For create, pass name and optional dashboard_id and activate. For read, pass optional dashboard_id; omitted dashboard_id targets the current dashboard. For update, pass name; omitted dashboard_id resolves to the current dashboard the same way read does.
